description: Drop one descriptor from each pair with |r|>0.95 (greedy, computed on the training fold) and drop constant descriptor columns, applying the same column mask to the test features while keeping the Morgan block intact.

Pick LightGBM and CatBoost iteration counts with an inner Murcko-scaffold GroupShuffleSplit (20% held out, AUC early stopping at lr 0.03, budget 1500), then refit each on the full training data with the chosen count while the RF and rank average stay unchanged.

Standardize each molecule (largest fragment, neutralize, fall back to the original), then rank-average five members: RF, LightGBM, CatBoost, a Tanimoto kNN (k=10, similarity-weighted) on binary Morgan bits, and a 3-seed MLP on quantile-scaled descriptors.

Standardize each molecule (largest fragment, neutralize, fall back to the original), then rank-average five members: RF, LightGBM, CatBoost, a Tanimoto kNN (k=10, similarity-weighted) on binary Morgan bits, and a 3-seed MLP on quantile-scaled descriptors.
Drop the RandomForestClassifier member, its import and its settings constants, and rank-average only LightGBM and CatBoost on the unchanged descriptor plus Morgan-count features.
Switch the LightGBM member to LightGBM's dart booster (drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, learning_rate=0.1), leaving the RF and CatBoost members and the rank average unchanged.

Append generic Murcko scaffold features (one-hot over the 512 most frequent training generic scaffolds, plus ring-system and scaffold-ring counts) to the existing descriptor and Morgan features, with the models unchanged.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes how the ensemble members' predictions are combined: it averages their logits instead of their normalized ranks. It touches no files, pastes no answers and uses no test labels.

No bug. Clipping at 1e-6 keeps the logit finite, and the sigmoid of the mean logit is a valid class-1 probability. The old rank average also worked for AUROC, but its outputs were not true probabilities.
Recomputed z with one run on each side and per-run sd 0.0049: (0.0942 - 0.0936) / (0.0049 * sqrt(2)) = 0.0006 / 0.00693 = 0.087. This matches the reported value.
A gain of 0.0006 is far below the noise, so the provisional reject is correct. If anything, the logit version is the cleaner of the two, so either choice is fine on code-simplicity grounds.

description: Replace the rank-average of the RF, LightGBM and CatBoost probabilities with the sigmoid of the mean log-odds, after clipping each member's probabilities to [1e-6, 1-1e-6].

Add balanced class weighting to every ensemble member (RF, LightGBM and CatBoost class weights, plus minority oversampling to parity for the MLP, with kNN left unweighted) on top of the standardized-molecule pipeline and the kNN and MLP members.

Make LightGBM and CatBoost shallower and more regularized (LightGBM: 8 leaves, reg_lambda 5, min_child_samples 20, 500 trees at lr 0.03; CatBoost: depth 4, l2_leaf_reg 10, 800 iterations at lr 0.03), keeping the RF and the rank average unchanged.

Adds a fourth rank-averaged member, a CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, 500 iterations, lr 0.05, rsm 0.2) trained with RMSE on the 0/1 labels smoothed to 0.05/0.95, to test whether a regression target on the same features adds diversity to the RF/LightGBM/CatBoost ensemble.
Append Gasteiger charge summary statistics and top-20 Crippen atom-type counts to the descriptor and Morgan features (not implemented: aborted before spending a slot).
Swap the LightGBM member for a seeded DART booster with extra trees (400 trees, learning rate 0.08, 15 leaves, drop rate 0.1) and keep the rank average.

Retune the CatBoost member to a shallower, more regularized model (depth 4, 900 iterations at learning rate 0.03, l2_leaf_reg 8, rsm 0.15, bagging_temperature 1.0), leaving features, the other two members and the rank average unchanged.
Set the CatBoost member to bootstrap_type='Bayesian' with bagging_temperature=1.0 explicitly, keeping all other settings and the rank average unchanged.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement. The candidate uses the test molecules' SMILES and features, but never their labels. The pseudo-labels come from the models' own rank agreement: all three models must put a molecule in the top quartile (>=0.75) or the bottom quartile (<=0.25). This is ordinary transductive self-training. It only uses inputs that fit_predict is given, and it works the same way on the final held-out test molecules.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The ranks rankdata(...)/len(Xt) fall in (0,1], so the quartile thresholds are valid. The label mapping is correct: top becomes 1, bottom becomes 0. The data are stacked correctly, and the seed is passed through. The second round refits all three models on train plus pseudo-labelled test, then ranks the full test set again.
Cost: each fit trains every model twice, so the job takes about twice as long. The job should still stay well under the 10-minute limit, but this adds complexity for no gain.

The numbers support the reject. Candidate 0.0947 against incumbent 0.0942 is a gap of 0.0005, slightly worse and far inside the noise (sd about 0.0049). Recomputed z = (0.0942-0.0947)/(0.0049*sqrt(2)) ≈ -0.072. This matches the harness's -0.067 up to rounding of the displayed values. Rejecting is correct: the gain is zero or negative and the code is more complex.

description: Pseudo-label self-training: after the first rank-averaged ensemble pass, add test molecules that all three models place in the same top or bottom quartile as hard-labelled training rows, refit the ensemble, and return the rank average of the refit predictions.

Adopt the standardization (largest fragment plus uncharging, with fallback) and add Tanimoto kNN and MLP rank-average members, then make LightGBM and CatBoost shallower and more regularized, keeping the equal-weight five-member blend and seed plumbing.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The code does not touch files or the network and does not paste in answers. The kNN only looks up train_y for training neighbours. The QuantileTransformer is fit on the training fold only. The test molecules are used only as inputs, never as labels.

Recomputed z: candidate mean (0.087+0.0804)/2 = 0.0837, incumbent 0.0942, gap 0.0105. SE = 0.0049*sqrt(1/2+1/1) = 0.0060, so z ≈ 1.75. The reported 1.741 is close, probably because the shown values are rounded. The two candidate runs differ by 0.0066, which fits the stated noise. The incumbent has only one run, so the comparison rests on few runs. z of about 1.75 is borderline, and one confirmation replicate would be worth spending.

Possible bug: B = X[:, n_desc:] assumes featurize puts the descriptors before the fingerprint in each row. The concatenation line is not shown in the diff. If the fingerprint comes first, the Tanimoto kNN runs on the tail of the fingerprint plus the binarised descriptors. The result would be weaker but still valid. Check the column order.
The QuantileTransformer and MLP are fed raw descriptor columns. NaN or inf values could crash some folds, but the runs finished, so it is not a problem in practice.

Complexity: this diff adds 5 changes at once (standardisation, kNN, MLP, and new GBM and CatBoost settings). That cuts against 'simpler is better', and we can't tell which part gives the gain. Ablating them later would show which parts are needed.

Retune only the LightGBM member to a shallower, more regularized setup (700 trees at learning rate 0.03, 15 leaves, min_child_samples 20, reg_lambda 5.0, subsample 0.7, colsample 0.2) while keeping features, the RF and CatBoost members, and the rank average unchanged.
Weight each training molecule by 1/sqrt(count of its Murcko scaffold in the training fold), normalized to mean 1, and pass it as sample_weight to the RF, LightGBM and CatBoost fits.
